body:
*Written by Claude*

## Purpose

With the carbon pools (`PrognosticCarbonModel`) feeding litter into the soil, the default
DAMM parameters leave soil organic carbon (SOC) without a steady state over much of the
land. With the Michaelis constant `michaelis_constant` at 0.0416 kg C m⁻³, the microbial
source Sm saturates at SOC far below observed values, and the litter of productive soils
exceeds that saturated rate, so SOC grows without bound. In a spin-up at the 1850 CO2
level with CRU-JRA forcing and the pools at equilibrium, 71% of the litter (48 Pg C/yr)
goes to layers where it exceeds the saturated rate, and SOC rises by 17–19 Pg C/yr
after 40 years. With the new values, SOC still rises in runs from the solved steady
state: by 3.1 Pg C/yr in a first 20-year run and by 2.1 Pg C/yr after a second solve,
almost all of it below 1 m in the tropics (see the caveats).

This PR:

- raises `soilCO2_reference_rate` from 3.34e-8 to 6.7e-7 kg C m⁻³ s⁻¹ (×20) and
  `michaelis_constant` from 0.0416 to 0.70 kg C m⁻³ (×16.8) together. The rate at low SOC
  (∝ V_ref/kM) rises by 19%; the saturated rate rises 20 times;
- adds the `slit` diagnostic (soil litter input, kg C m⁻³ s⁻¹) for a `LandModel` with
  carbon pools;
- adds norms from the review to `AGENTS.md`: reuse ClimaAnalysis and ClimaCore before
  writing helpers, keep scientific assumptions out of plotting functions, compute depth
  integrals in the model, and register conditional diagnostics with `add_diagnostics!`;
- removes `CLAUDE.md`, which only imported `AGENTS.md`: Claude Code reads `AGENTS.md`
  directly since v2.1.277.

An earlier version of this PR also added a leaderboard figure comparing the steady-state
SOC with SoilGrids. That comparison stays only with the spun-up pre-industrial SOC in
ClimaArtifacts.

## Results

The "long run opt lai" configuration (`snowy_land_pmodel.jl` with prognostic LAI,
2008-03 to 2011-03, SOC initialized from SoilGrids, scored over the last year), run on
Derecho with the old and new values. GPP and the ERA5 energy-flux scores are identical.

| | old | new | target |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPP (Pg C/yr) | 144.7 | 144.7 | 138.7 (inversion 2002–2020) |
| Rh (Pg C/yr) | 35.0 | 65.4 | 51.9 |
| ER (Pg C/yr) | 117.0 | 147.4 | 135.2 |
| NEE (Pg C/yr) | −27.7 | +2.7 | −3.5 |
| litter / Sm (Pg C/yr) | 63.5 / 36.0 | 63.5 / 66.8 | |
| ER bias, RMSE (g m⁻² d⁻¹) | −0.20, 1.16 | +0.42, 1.36 | against FlagshipCarbonMetrics |
| NEE bias, RMSE (g m⁻² d⁻¹) | −0.44, 0.99 | +0.11, 0.76 | |

With the old values, SOC at the SoilGrids level decomposes at about half the litter
input, so the soil takes up 28 Pg C/yr. The new values bring Sm close to the litter, and
NEE close to the inversion. ER is higher than the leaderboard's product mostly because
GPP is (ER bias − GPP bias ≈ NEE bias: 0.42 − 0.29 ≈ 0.11).

The prescribed-LAI long run (`snowy_land_pmodel.jl`, 2008-03 to 2010-03, no carbon pools,
SOC initialized from SoilGrids, scored over the last year) improves as well. GPP and the
ERA5 energy-flux scores are again identical.

| | old | new | target |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPP (Pg C/yr) | 138.2 | 138.2 | 138.7 (inversion 2002–2020) |
| Rh (Pg C/yr) | 33.9 | 65.1 | 51.9 |
| ER (Pg C/yr) | 104.6 | 135.8 | 135.2 |
| NEE (Pg C/yr) | −33.6 | −2.4 | −3.5 |
| ER bias, RMSE (g m⁻² d⁻¹) | −0.42, 1.36 | +0.21, 1.26 | against FlagshipCarbonMetrics |
| NEE bias, RMSE (g m⁻² d⁻¹) | −0.55, 1.30 | +0.02, 0.91 | |

The "long run opt lai" job of this PR's Buildkite build
([climaland-long-runs #5172](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaland-long-runs/builds/5172))
reproduces the ER and NEE scores of the "new" column.

## How the values were chosen

From a spin-up at the 1850 CO2 level with CRU-JRA forcing (1901–1920 recycled) and the
carbon pools at equilibrium (wood 176 Pg C), on a study branch that is not part of this
PR. Over a 20-year cycle I accumulated each layer's mean litter and its time-mean Sm on
a grid of SOC values, then solved each layer's steady state for candidate parameters,
and matched SoilGrids' top metre on the model grid (2,112 Pg C). With V_ref ×20, that
takes kM ×16.8. At the steady state:

- SOC is 2,104 Pg C over 0–1 m and 2,869 over 0–2 m (SoilGrids: 2,112 and 2,960). By
  band, the ratios to SoilGrids are 0.86 north of 50°N, 1.34 for 30–50°N, 0.95 in the
  tropics and 0.93 south of 30°S;
- the litter with no steady state falls from 32 to 0.12 Pg C/yr in the top metre (1.27
  over all depths; the verification run below confirms it);
- the mean turnover time of the top metre is 48 years.

The activation energy (19,800 J mol⁻¹, Q10 ≈ 1.3), `O2_michaelis_constant` and
`oxygen_diffusion_coefficient` are unchanged: a higher activation energy worsened the
tropics, and the other two mattered little. Smaller V_ref multipliers fit the bands no
better and leave 1–24 Pg C/yr of litter with no steady state.

## Caveats

- The old values came from the calibration in
  `experiments/calibration/configs/gpp_er_nee_lhf.jl`. In both LAI modes, Rh at
  SoilGrids' SOC roughly doubles with the new values. The prescribed-LAI numbers above
  are from my runs on Derecho; I left the "Run long runs" label to you. In that mode, Rh
  is now above the inversion's and Ra (70.7 Pg C/yr) below its implied 83, so ER is
  right for partly offsetting reasons.
- The values were tuned to the 1850 equilibrium. The litter in the long runs above is
  present-day (2010 forcing at about 387 ppm), 1.35 times the 1850 litter.
- In dry grasslands (the US Great Plains, the Central Asian steppe, the Pampas) Sm is
  strongly moisture-limited and the steady state is high.
- Saturated layers below 1 m have no O2 and no anaerobic pathway, so the litter they
  receive (1.3 to 1.9 Pg C/yr in successive solves) has no steady state.
- A 20-year verification run from the solved state (1850 CO2, CRU-JRA 1901–1920
  recycled) drifts more than the solve predicts. NBP averages 3.1 Pg C/yr with no decay
  over the 20 years, and SOC rises by 3.1 Pg C/yr (1.3 in the top metre, 0.06% per year
  of the top-metre stock). Of this, 1.2 Pg C/yr goes to the layers the solve found
  without a steady state, as predicted. The other 1.9 Pg C/yr goes to layers with a
  steady state, nearly three-quarters of it in the tropics, at a rate that does not
  decay. The method itself holds: over one year of a later cycle, the curves evaluated
  at the run's SOC reproduce its Sm within 0.3%. So the gap comes from the state changing
  between the cycle the curves came from, run with the old values, and the verification.
  Soil O2, which is prognostic and consumed by Sm, is one candidate: Sm was a third lower
  in that cycle, and the layers where O2 fell between the two cycles (at the end of the
  same forcing year) carry 1.2 of the 1.9 Pg C/yr. The other 0.8 is in layers where O2
  did not change, and the soil physics also still changes between cycles: under the same
  weather, the top metre holds 0.5% less liquid water than one cycle earlier.
- A second cycle and a second solve, on curves from a cycle run with the new values,
  narrow the drift to the deep tropics. The second 20-year verification run averages
  2.1 Pg C/yr of NBP. SOC in the top metre rises by 0.3 Pg C/yr (0.01% of its stock per
  year); below 1 m it rises by 1.8 Pg C/yr, as in every cycle (1.82, 1.81 and 1.76 in
  three cycles): in tropical layers at 1–4 m, root litter enters faster than
  respiration, capped by its saturated rate and by O2, removes it. The litter going to
  layers with no steady state grows with each solve (1.3, 1.7, 1.9 Pg C/yr), and each
  solve adds about 400 Pg C there, so the steady state below 1 m is not pinned down. In
  the top metre it is: on the curves of the two later cycles, matching SoilGrids' top
  metre needs `michaelis_constant` ×0.98 and ×0.96, so 0.70 holds there. Below 1 m in
  the tropics, the spin-up does not reach a steady state with these values.

title: Raise the DAMM rate and Michaelis constant so soil carbon reaches a steady state
